title: How Many Knibis to BEAT Stockfish?
summary: Odds series vs Fairy-Stockfish level 8 (lichess-style UI): narrator has only his king + N Knibis (start 1, +1 after each loss) vs a simplified black army (the variant's own fairy pieces on the minor-piece squares were removed, leaving K, Q, 2R and pawns). Knibis = moves like a knight, captures like a bishop. He loses with 1-9 knibis and finally wins with 10 knibis by keeping them mutually defended on mixed colours and mating with a knibis on b7. Post-game eval: 5 knibis still losing, 6 knibis already ~+3 for white; Stockfish places them on the edges facing inward.
rules: Knibis: non-capturing moves = knight jumps; captures = bishop slides (diagonal any distance). It cannot defend/capture orthogonally-adjacent or knight squares.
Player: king + N knibis, N starts at 1 and +1 after each loss; no pawns (frame with 8 knibis shows a full back rank of knibis and no pawns).
Engine (black): standard army minus minor pieces (K, Q, 2R, 8 pawns) - 'originally there were other fairy pieces on these squares... I've simplified the black position'.
Normal chess rules; stalemate is a draw.
win_condition: Checkmate Fairy-Stockfish. Took 10 knibis in the video.
